title: Historical Mean / True / Sheeghroccheya evidence ledger

annualCoverage.note: The annual runner records 3,000 finite candidate rows but explicitly leaves independentHistoricalOracleVerified false for every random epoch.

meanSourceAudit.source: Burgess 1860, pp.164–165, Bīja-corrected mean-motion and 1 Jan 1860 Ujjain mean-longitude tables.

trueLongitudeAudit.source: Burgess 1860 Sūrya-Siddhānta II.39–45; B.V. Raman Ch.VI §§99–107, pp.74–79.
trueLongitudeAudit.modernReference: NASA/JPL Horizons DE441 Earth-geocentric apparent ecliptic-of-date, quantity 31, explicit Saura frame transfer.
trueLongitudeAudit.note: 3,000 January annual checkpoints are modern numerical comparisons, not the 600 random DOB epochs or historical classical printed-table oracles.

sheeghroccheyaAudit.conflict: Saturn §104 table p.77: 151.23°; Example 49 p.78: 181.23°, yielding 63.42° Chesta Kendra and 21.14 Chesta Bala.
sheeghroccheyaAudit.limit: One worked example only; no complete 1800–2399 independent tabulation acquired.

independentEphemerisAcquisition.officialMetadata: IMD PAC identifies modern IAE reference epoch J2000.5 and ephemeris argument TT.
independentEphemerisAcquisition.note: Actual government 1971/1974 IENA and 1992/1994/2015 IAE daily rows remain unacquired. Additionally, a searchable full-text scan of N.C. Lahiri's separate 1974 private Nirayana ephemeris was found. It specifies daily geocentric apparent Nirayana positions at 0h UT (05:30 IST) and separate mean positions on printed p.33, but OCR row/column alignment is insufficient for numeric transcription.

alternate1974LahiriAnnualEphemeris.title: Indian Ephemeris of Planets’ Positions According to the Nirayana or Indian System for 1974
alternate1974LahiriAnnualEphemeris.author: Nirmal Chandra Lahiri
alternate1974LahiriAnnualEphemeris.sourceIdentity: Private annual Nirayana ephemeris; not the Government of India Indian Ephemeris and Nautical Almanac (IENA).

documentedContents.dailyPlanetLongitudes: Geocentric apparent Nirayana longitudes for Sun, Moon and planets
documentedContents.dailyEpoch: 0h Universal Time / 0h GMT, stated equivalent to 05:30 IST
documentedContents.separateMeanPositions: Mean positions provided separately on printed page 33
documentedContents.otherEpoch: Latitudes, declinations, heliocentric longitudes and right ascensions at 0h Ephemeris Time

alternate1974LahiriAnnualEphemeris.sourceEvidenceLocator: Title and publisher: extracted lines 154–205. Daily ephemeris time/frame description: lines 288–318. Daily table headings and May 1974 monthly table: lines 2216–2242. October 1974 table heading: lines 4066–4102.
alternate1974LahiriAnnualEphemeris.reasonNotNumericallyCertified: The web text extraction has lost row/column alignment in the numeric monthly tables; exact day/planet cells cannot safely be attributed from this OCR alone.
alternate1974LahiriAnnualEphemeris.use: Potential independent sidereal apparent-longitude spot-check after obtaining a legible page scan; do not blend its Nirayana zero point or UT/ET epochs into the Burgess Saura chain.

rows.sourceLocator: E. Burgess, Translation of the Sūrya-Siddhānta (1860), Bīja-corrected mean tables, pp.164–165; B.V. Raman, Graha and Bhava Balas, Ch.VI §§94–98, pp.72–74.
rows.method: Burgess Bīja-corrected revolutions and B.V. Raman tabular mean daily motions; 1918 value is one worked-example anchor.
rows.notes: 1860 Ujjain-midnight source-table regression max residual 0.9674 arcsec, tolerance 1.5 arcsec. Not an independent oracle for every random natal epoch.
